FetchCounters.description:
HTTP cache behaviour and transferred bytes (§14.3, §8.4).

The three cache outcomes are kept apart because they answer different questions. A `hit`
opened no socket at all. A `revalidated` opened one and the server said `304`, so the bytes
were reused but freshness was actually re-established. A `miss` transferred a body. Folding
the middle case into either of the others would misreport both cost and freshness.

**Read `hits` narrowly.** The service revalidates every stored `200` rather than serving it
blind, so a reused *representation* shows up as `revalidated`, not as a hit. The only thing
that increments `hits` is the bounded negative cache — a recent `404`/`410` reused within
`freshness.negative_cache_ttl_seconds`. `hits + revalidated` is the number an operator
probably means by "the cache worked"; `hits` alone is "we did not even ask".

revalidated.description: Requests where validators matched and the origin returned `304`.

lsp.description:
Language-server starts, reuses and evictions in this daemon process.

Published because gate C17 -- "inspection does not start an LSP unnecessarily" -- is only
checkable against a counter. A caller reading `started` before and after a signature-only
inspection can see for itself that nothing was started. Blueprint §14.3 asks for the same
numbers as operational metrics.

Every counter beside it is scoped to that window. Without this an operator reading
`fetch.misses = 3` cannot tell a quiet hour from a daemon that restarted a minute ago.

enabled_profiles.description:
Profiles configuration has enabled.

Read from `LIBENR_CONFIG`; `enabled_profiles_source` names the file, or says these are
built-in defaults. A caller selects from this list and never grants itself permission.

enabled_profiles_source.description: Where `enabled_profiles` came from, so a caller is never misled about policy.

execution_qualified.description:
Whether an actual containment run has qualified the configured execution images.

Three different facts live next to each other here on purpose: a profile can be
*enabled*, a runtime can be *present*, and images can be *configured*, and none of the
three means the service can contain anything. Only `execution_qualified` says that, and
it is set only by a receipt from `just execution-qualify`.

execution_readiness.description: When qualification happened and against which images, or the missing prerequisite.

execution_routes.description:
Implemented execution routes assessed by the same admission logic used by tools.
Empty when no running service is available to assess qualification and cleanup.

accepts.description: Every version this daemon can accept.

emits.description: The version emitted on every response.

Scope.description: Independent axes of a release comparison, with one native evidence policy.

kind.description:
The kinds of evidence a producer can require or yield, and that `coverage.indexed` and
`coverage.missing` name.

The values are, in order: `registry_metadata`, `crate_source`,
`documentation_build_config`, `hosted_rustdoc_json`, `public_api`, `documentation`,
`examples`, `release_notes`, `source_excerpts`.

snapshot_id.description: Names one immutable set of evidence available for a context.

witness_id.description: A qualified fact establishing the selected state. Historical attempts remain retained.

ScopeState.description: Unknown means no qualified coverage fact exists; it is distinct from a declared gap.

area.description: Namespace subtree that was searched, when requested.

page.description: Bounded page over this payload, not over the whole research envelope.

scoring.description: The scoring legend, in rank order.

tokens.description: The tokens it was split into.

also_at.description: Other public paths to the same definition.

evidence_id.description: The evidence entry this hit is cited by.

area.description: Restrict symbol/fragment subjects to this namespace subtree.

max_bytes.description: Byte budget for the page; the configured inline budget bounds it.

max_items.description: Page size; the configured limit bounds it.

snapshot_id.description: A specific snapshot; the context's current one when omitted.

SingleFlightCounts.description: Producer runs started and callers served by a shared run (§8.2, gate C04).

inflight.description: Distinct pieces of work running right now.

shared.description: Callers that attached to a run someone else started.

started.description: Producer runs this process actually started.

total_millis.description:
Total wall time spent inside producer work, across every started run.

Summed rather than averaged: a mean loses the one run that took a minute, and §14.3 wants
a diagnostic, not a statistic. Divide by `started` if a mean is what you want.

SnapshotCounts.description: Counts an overview and a manifest report.

producer_items.description: Items the producer saw in total, including those not surfaced as symbols.

reexports.description: Paths that re-export a definition reachable elsewhere.

unresolved_reexports.description: Re-exports whose target is outside this crate.

SnapshotDescriptor.description: Small snapshot publication metadata. Release/environment records belong to catalog Parquet.

context_id.description: Binds a release to an environment and a research mode.

ecosystem.description:
Which package ecosystem a release belongs to.

The values are, in order: `rust`, `python`. No variant carries a doc comment -- see the
module docs in [`crate::wire`].

environment_id.description: Identifies the declared or resolved environment.

release_id.description:
Identifies the actual library release: ecosystem, registry, package, exact version and
the selected artifact digest.

SnapshotSummary.description: What the published snapshot holds, summarized.

SourceExcerpt.description: A bounded source excerpt starting at a recorded line; it does not identify the end of an item.

path.description: The file, relative to the crate root.

truncated.description: Whether the file had more lines after `end_line`.

features.description: Optional capabilities and whether each is supported.

producers.description: Evidence producers and whether each is installed.

sandbox.description: Which execution profiles are actually usable here.

schema_compatibility.description: Which wire schema versions this daemon can speak.

snapshot_compatibility.description: On-disk storage compatibility; independent of the MCP response envelope.

SubjectRef.description: A reference carries its indexing domain. External paths never masquerade as local keys.

release_id.description:
Identifies the actual library release: ecosystem, registry, package, exact version and
the selected artifact digest.

SymbolHeader.description:
Public binding identity. Observed signatures, documentation and source coordinates
remain in independently qualified observations, never synthesized into this header.

kind.description: Declaration kind, shared by native fields, admission and generated wire enums.

TargetRef.description: Relationship target domains, including legitimate unresolved targets.

TerminalOutcome.description: Only terminal states are representable; a failure always carries its typed diagnostic.

TextFragment.description: Text evidence keeps its typed subject and exact acquisition qualification at every boundary.

kind.description: What kind of text a fragment is.

UpstreamCheck.description: What the registry says about newer releases, kept separate from what was resolved.

newest_any.description: Newest non-yanked version of any kind.

published_versions.description: Number of published versions the index listed.

resolved_is_newest_stable.description: Whether the resolved version is the newest stable one.

VerificationCounters.description:
How verification work finished (§9.3, §14.3).

`unresolved` is its own outcome rather than a kind of failure: a probe the service could not
run -- an unqualified image, an unavailable profile -- says nothing about the code under
test, and counting it as a failure would overstate what was observed.

failed.description: Probes that ran and failed, which is an observation about the code.

unresolved.description: Probes that could not be run, which is an observation about the service.

VerificationData.description: Scoped consumer verification; original static evidence remains independently readable.

derived_snapshot_id.description: Names one immutable set of evidence available for a context.

evidence_class.description:
The six epistemic classes (blueprint §6.2).

These are categories, not a confidence scale. An API signature can be `compiler_derived`
while "this replaces our orchestration layer" is `agent_inferred`, and the two never merge.

The values are, in order: `declared`, `statically_extracted`, `compiler_derived`,
`typechecker_observed`, `runtime_observed`, `agent_inferred`.

No variant carries a doc comment -- see the module docs in [`super`](crate::wire).

profile.description:
The three execution profiles (§10).

The values are, in order: `static`, `build`, `runtime`.

source_context_id.description: Binds a release to an environment and a research mode.

source_snapshot_id.description: Names one immutable set of evidence available for a context.

VerifyRequest.description: Exact consumer input, pinned to a snapshot before scheduling.

profile.description:
The three execution profiles (§10).

The values are, in order: `static`, `build`, `runtime`.

snapshot_id.description: Names one immutable set of evidence available for a context.

Versions.description: Versions of the daemon and its toolchain.

schema.description: The wire schema version this build emits.

WorkerFile.description: One source file selected by Rust for the static worker.

description:
The response envelope every tool returns.

`status`, `job` and `error` are private: [`Envelope::new`] and the [`Outcome`] enum are the
only way to populate them, which is what makes the cross-field rule a type-level fact rather
than a convention.

coverage.description: What was looked at, and what was not.

schema_version.description: The epoch selected by the current native envelope declaration.

status.description:
The four result statuses (blueprint §7.2).

The values are, in order: `ok`, `partial`, `pending`, `error`. `ok` means successful within
the declared coverage, not complete knowledge; `partial` carries usable evidence *and* gaps.

No variant carries a doc comment -- see the module docs in [`super`](crate::wire).

summary.description: One-line account of what this result establishes.
